answer: The garden multiplier is published, charged in comet, and mirror lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3761 identities would post 670 proofs and burn roughly 63 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
